source.title: Packings and coverings of groups: some results and open problems

accepted.question_text: Let G be an infinite group. For a subset A of G, let pack(A) be the supremum of the cardinalities of families of pairwise disjoint left translates of A, and let Pack(G) be the set of all values pack(A) as A ranges over subsets of G. Is every infinite cardinal kappa with aleph_0 <= kappa <= |G| an element of Pack(G)?
accepted.context_brief: Packing spectrum of an infinite group

evidence.quote: pack(A) = sup{|S|: S ⊆ G, {sA: s ∈ S} is disjoint},
Problem 1. Is it true that [ℵ0, G] ⊆ Pack(G) for every infinite group G?

accepted.question_text: Let G be an infinite group, and let Pack(G) be the set of all packing numbers pack(A) realized by subsets A of G, where pack(A) measures the largest cardinality of a family of pairwise disjoint left translates of A. Is there a finite exceptional set of finite cardinals such that every other finite cardinal belongs to Pack(G)?
accepted.context_brief: Finite values in the packing spectrum

evidence.quote: pack(A) = sup{|S|: S ⊆ G, {sA: s ∈ S} is disjoint},
Problem 2. Let G be an infinite group. Does Pack(G) contain all but finitely many finite cardinals?

accepted.question_text: Let G be an infinite group. For a subset A of G, let cov(A) be the least cardinality of a set S of group elements such that G = SA, and let Cov(G) be the set of all values cov(A) as A ranges over subsets of G. Is Cov(G) exactly the whole cardinal interval [1, |G|], meaning that every cardinal kappa with 1 <= kappa <= |G| occurs as cov(A) for some subset A of G?
accepted.context_brief: Covering spectrum of an infinite group

evidence.quote: cov(A) = min{|S|: S ⊆ G, G = SA}.
Problem 3. Is it true that Cov(G) = [1, |G|] for every infinite group G?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a group. For each subset A of G, let pack(A) be its packing number and cov(A) its covering number. Suppose that every subset A of G with finite pack(A) satisfies pack(A) <= cov(A). Must G be an amenable group?
accepted.context_brief: Amenability detected by packing and covering

evidence.quote: pack(A) = sup{|S|: S ⊆ G, {sA: s ∈ S} is disjoint}, cov(A) = min{|S|: S ⊆ G, G = SA}.
Problem 4. Is a group G amenable provided that pack(S) 6 cov(S) for every subset S of G with finite pack(S)?

accepted.question_text: Let G be an infinite group with identity element e. A subset A of G is 2-thin if |gA ∩ A| <= 2 for every g in G with g != e. A subset A is self-linked if pack(A) = 1, equivalently if gA ∩ A is nonempty for every g in G, or equivalently if G = AA^{-1}. Does every infinite group G contain a subset A that is both 2-thin and self-linked?

evidence.quote: For a natural number k, it is more convenient to say that a subset A of G is k-thin if |gA ∩ A| 6 k for every g ∈ G, g 6= e.
A subset A of a group G is called self–linked if pack(A) = 1, equivalently, gA ∩ A 6= ∅ for every g ∈ G (or G = AA−1).
Problem 5. Has every infinite group G a 2-thin self–linked subset?

accepted.question_text: Consider the additive group of real numbers R. For a natural number k, call a subset A of R k-thin if |(g + A) ∩ A| <= k for every nonzero real number g. Can R be partitioned into aleph_0 subsets so that each cell of the partition is k-thin for some natural number k that may depend on the cell? More strongly, does there exist a single natural number k such that R can be partitioned into aleph_0 subsets that are all k-thin? Finally, can R be partitioned into aleph_0 subsets each of which is linearly independent over Q, a condition that makes each subset 1-thin?
accepted.context_brief: Countable partitions of the real line into thin subsets

evidence.quote: For a natural number k, it is more convenient to say that a subset A of G is k-thin if |gA ∩ A| 6 k for every g ∈ G, g 6= e.

Problem 6. Can R be partitioned in ℵ0 subsets such that each subset of the partition is k-thin for some k? Does there exist k ∈ N such that R can be partitioned in ℵ0 k-thin subsets? Can R be partitioned in ℵ0 subsets linearly independent over Q (each such subset is 1-thin)?
